title: Advanced Hunting, Threat Analytics and Hunting Graphs

header.html: Interpret threat analytics in Microsoft Defender XDR; create hunting graphs, including blast radius; analyze relationships between entities by using Sentinel Graph; create Advanced Hunting queries
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

html:
1Advanced hunting in Defender XDR

Advanced hunting is the query-based hunting tool of the Defender portal: Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting.

Quota or limit Value
Data range 30 days for native Defender data; Sentinel tables follow their analytics-tier retention
Result set 100,000 rows per query
Timeout 10 minutes per query
Result size 64 MB
CPU Allocation by tenant size, refreshed every 15 minutes; usage shown as Low, Medium, High; a warning appears above 10% and the query is blocked at 100% until the next cycle
Freshness Event tables are near real time; entity tables refresh every hour

Keep data longer than 30 days by onboarding a Sentinel workspace and setting the analytics-tier retention, or by streaming through the Defender streaming API. Data stored only in the Sentinel data lake is not in advanced hunting; use data lake exploration (Module 18).

Access Fact
Full read Global Administrator, Security Administrator, Security Reader, Global Reader
Unified RBAC Raw data > Email & collaboration metadata (read) for email tables; Security data basics (read) for alerts and behaviors
Endpoint tables Governed by Defender for Endpoint RBAC and device groups

Query resources report: shows the resource use of queries (last day by default); Security Reader or higher sees all users; states completed, failed, throttled.

2Saving and sharing queries

Where Use
My queries Private to you
Shared queries Whole organization; chosen with Save query > Save as
Community queries From the GitHub Azure-Sentinel repository, reviewed before publishing

Share link copies a direct link. Deleting a saved query is permanent. Functions you can call in a query include FileProfile() (file prevalence and signer data), DeviceFromIP() (which device had an IP) and AssignedIPAddresses() (IPs of a device at a time) [Verify live]. Save a query as a custom detection (Module 9) when it should run on a schedule.

Exam tip

. 30 days, 100,000 rows, 10 minutes. For longer history, connect Sentinel and set retention.

3Threat analytics

Threat analytics is the threat intelligence feature of Defender XDR: reports on active threat actors, techniques and vulnerabilities, with your exposure and your protection. Dashboard: security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3.

Dashboard section Shows
Latest threats Newest reports with active and resolved alert counts
High-impact threats Reports with the most active and resolved alerts
Highest exposure threats Reports with the greatest exposure (vulnerable and misconfigured devices)
Report tab Content
Overview Charts (related incidents, alerts over time, impacted assets, recommended actions, endpoint exposure) and metadata (aliases, origin, targets, MITRE ATT&CK techniques)
Analyst report Executive summary, overview, detections and hunting queries, techniques, recommendations, references, change log
Related incidents, Impacted assets Your incidents and assets tied to the threat
Endpoints exposure, Recommended actions Vulnerable devices and mitigations (tracked in Secure Score)
Indicators (preview) IOCs updated in real time

Report types: Activity (a campaign), Actor (a Microsoft-tracked threat actor), Core threat, Technique (one ATT&CK technique), Tool, Vulnerability (a CVE or group), OSINT (preview). Tags: Ransomware, Phishing, Activity group, Vulnerability.

Access Fact
License At least one Defender product; Defender for Endpoint Plan 1 does not grant access
Roles Security data basics (read) for reports, incidents and assets; Vulnerability management (read) and Exposure Management (read) for exposure data
Link a rule A custom detection rule can be linked to a report; its alerts then show under Related incidents
Agent The Threat Intelligence Briefing Agent shows a banner on the page
Exam tip

. Threat analytics tells you whether a threat affects you. Related incidents = you are already hit. Endpoints exposure = you could be hit.

4The hunting graph

The hunting graph shows entities as nodes (devices, accounts, IPs) and relationships as edges. Open Advanced hunting, then the hunting graph icon or Create new > Hunting graph.

Part Fact
Predefined scenarios For example Attack paths to critical asset, Entity relationship map, Paths between two entities, Potential data exfiltration by device, Paths to domain admins, Kerberoast paths to critical assets, OAuth applications with privileged access
Run Choose a scenario and inputs, set filters, select Run scenario
Filters Source node (is critical, is vulnerable, is exposed to the internet), target node (has sensitive data, has a risk score), edge type, edge direction, Show only the shortest paths
Prerequisites Roles as for advanced hunting, Sentinel data lake onboarding and at least read access in Microsoft Security Exposure Management

Blast radius (Module 13) is the same graph engine applied to an incident node.

5Microsoft Sentinel graph

Sentinel graph is unified graph analytics. It answers questions such as what is the blast radius of a compromised document.

Where it appears Feature
Defender portal Incident graph with blast radius; hunting graph
Purview Data risk graph in insider risk management and data security investigations
Custom graphs (preview) Author in a Jupyter notebook (VS Code extension), publish and materialize with a graph job, query with Graph Query Language (GQL) on the Graphs page

On-demand graph jobs keep the graph for 30 days; scheduled jobs rebuild on their schedule. It is billed by the Sentinel graph meter.

Exam tip

. Hunting graph = explore relationships and paths. Blast radius = from an incident node. Both need the Sentinel data lake.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A hunting query returns an error that it reached a limit. Which quota is possible?

  • A20 rows per query, or the 30 second timeout
  • B100,000 rows per query, or the 10 minute timeout
  • C1 million rows per query, or the 1 hour timeout limit
  • D5,000 rows per query, or the 2 minute timeout
Show the answer

Answer: B. Advanced hunting returns up to 100,000 rows and times out after 10 minutes.

S2A team needs to hunt over 180 days of Defender XDR data. Which approach meets the requirement?

  • AOnboard a Sentinel workspace and set the analytics-tier retention
  • BIncrease the advanced hunting date range in the portal settings page
  • CMove the tables to the data lake tier and query them in hunting
  • DExport the results every day to a spreadsheet for later review
Show the answer

Answer: A. Native data covers 30 days; a Sentinel workspace with analytics retention extends it. Data lake data is not in advanced hunting.

S3An analyst wants a hunting query to be available to every analyst in the organization. What should the analyst do?

  • ASave it under My queries and send the link by email
  • BSave it as a custom detection rule that runs every hour
  • CUse Save query, Save as, and choose Shared queries
  • DCopy it to a Community queries repository on GitHub
Show the answer

Answer: C. Shared queries are visible to the whole organization; My queries are private.

S4A new report on a ransomware campaign appears in threat analytics. The SOC wants to know which of its devices are vulnerable to the threat. Which tab helps?

  • AAnalyst report, which describes the campaign in text
  • BIndicators, which lists indicators of compromise
  • CRelated incidents, which lists incidents already raised
  • DEndpoints exposure, which shows vulnerable devices
Show the answer

Answer: D. Endpoints exposure shows exposure from vulnerabilities and affected devices; Related incidents shows incidents that already exist.

S5A hunter wants to see paths from internet-exposed vulnerable devices to critical assets. Which tool and scenario fit?

  • AThreat analytics, with the Analyst report tab
  • BAdvanced hunting, with the join operator on two tables
  • CThe incident queue, with a filter on critical assets
  • DThe hunting graph, with Attack paths to critical asset
Show the answer

Answer: D. The hunting graph has the predefined scenario Attack paths to critical asset with source filters such as is exposed to the internet.

S6Which license statement about threat analytics is correct?

  • AAny Microsoft 365 license gives access to every threat analytics report
  • BA license for at least one Defender product is needed, but Defender for Endpoint Plan 1 does not qualify
  • COnly Microsoft Sentinel customers can see the threat analytics dashboard
  • DDefender for Endpoint Plan 1 alone gives access to every report
Show the answer

Answer: B. Threat analytics needs a license for at least one Defender product; Defender for Endpoint P1 does not grant access.

6.2 Recall questions

R1How many rows can advanced hunting return?

Show the answer

100,000 per query.

R2What is the advanced hunting query timeout?

Show the answer

10 minutes.

R3Which report type describes a Microsoft-tracked threat actor?

Show the answer

Actor.

R4What language queries a custom Sentinel graph?

Show the answer

Graph Query Language (GQL).

R5How long does an on-demand graph job keep its graph?

Show the answer

30 days.

R6Which saved query location is private to you?

Show the answer

My queries.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Limits 30 days, 100,000 rows, 10 minutes, 64 MB
Longer history onboard Sentinel and set analytics retention; lake data is not in advanced hunting
Saved queries My, Shared (whole org), Community; deleting is permanent
Threat analytics dashboard sections, report types, exposure tabs; not included with Defender for Endpoint P1
Hunting graph nodes and edges, predefined scenarios, needs data lake and Exposure Management read
Sentinel graph blast radius, custom graphs with GQL, graph jobs
